title: Indian Startups Raised $274 Million This Week as Cleantech and AI Lead the Surge
excerpt: A 74% jump in weekly startup funding was driven by River Mobility's $120 million Series C and strong AI deal flow across 22 companies.
body:
• 22 Indian startups raised a combined $274.4 million between August 3-7, a 74% increase from the previous week's $142.3 million
  • River Mobility's $120 million Series C for electric vehicles was the week's largest round, making cleantech the most-funded segment
  • AI startups led deal count with seven companies raising $23.3 million across seed and Series A rounds

Indian startup funding surged in the first week of August, with 22 companies raising a combined $274.4 million — a 74% jump from $142.3 million across 11 deals in the previous week.

The sharp uptick was driven by a single blockbuster round: River Mobility's $120 million Series C, led by Elev8 Venture Partners and Claypond Capital, with participation from Yamaha Motor Corporation, Mitsui & Co., and several Indian institutional investors including HDFC AMC and 360 ONE Asset. The electric vehicle startup's raise made cleantech the week's most-funded sector, with four companies in the space collectively pulling in about $136 million.

AI Dominates Deal Flow

While cleantech claimed the dollar volume, AI dominated deal count. Seven AI startups raised $23.3 million during the week, ranging from Pinegap's $8 million Series A backed by Stellaris Venture Partners to seed rounds for Profound ($1.5 million) and NYAI ($1.5 million).

The AI deals reflect a growing pattern in India's startup ecosystem: application-layer AI companies — those building end-user products on top of foundation models — are attracting consistent early-stage capital. Superleap raised $4.2 million in a pre-Series A from Surge (Peak XV Partners), while Hulp pulled in $2.6 million in seed funding from Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures.

Other Notable Rounds

Beyond the top-line numbers, several rounds stood out:

InRisk Labs raised $27 million in a Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners for its insurtech platform. BlissClub, the D2C activewear brand, secured $16.8 million from Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures. HomeRun raised $12 million in a Series A from Nexus Venture Partners for its quick-commerce operations platform.

Mitti Labs, an agritech startup focused on modern farming, pulled in $9.5 million with Aramco Venture leading alongside Godrej Industries and Cisco Foundation — a signal that climate-adjacent agriculture is drawing serious institutional backing.

M&A and IPO Activity

The week also saw active deal-making on the M&A front. Times Network acquired fintech startup OpiGo, while Mintoak acquired Dubai-based ICC Loyalty to expand beyond merchant payments. Imarticus Learning acquired Singapore's BELLS Institute of Higher Learning for ₹800 crore ahead of its planned ₹1,000 crore IPO.

On the public markets side, SEBI cleared IPOs for Garuda Aerospace, PlaySimple Games, and Rediff. Shiprocket filed its Red Herring Prospectus to raise ₹1,617 crore, a 30% reduction from its earlier proposed size, with the issue set to open August 12. Spacetech unicorn Skyroot Aerospace invited bids for a $200 million fundraise at a $2 billion valuation, an 80% jump from its May valuation.

Investor Trends

DeVC was the week's most active investor, backing three startups. Singularity AMC and Stellaris Venture Partners each backed two companies. Seed-stage funding declined 35% week-on-week to $7.7 million across five deals, suggesting early-stage investors may be growing more selective even as later-stage capital flows freely.

The week's funding pace, if sustained, would put August on track to be one of the strongest months for Indian startup funding in 2026 — a contrast to the cautious fundraising environment that characterized much of 2024 and early 2025.
